questions.text: Which sentence correctly uses an APOSTROPHE to show possession?
options: The ranchers horses needed water.
The rancher's horses needed water.
The ranchers' horse's needed water.
The ranchers horses' needed water.
questions.answer: The rancher's horses needed water.

questions.text: Which sentence correctly shows PLURAL possession (belonging to more than one farmer)?
options: The farmer's fields were flooded.
The farmers field's were flooded.
The farmers' fields were flooded.
The farmer's' fields were flooded.
questions.answer: The farmers' fields were flooded.

questions.text: Which sentence is in the FUTURE tense?
options: She milked the cows at dawn.
She milks the cows every morning.
She will milk the cows tomorrow.
She has milked the cows before.
questions.answer: She will milk the cows tomorrow.

questions.text: Which sentence uses a CONJUNCTION to combine two independent clauses CORRECTLY?
options: The drought was severe but the farmers kept working.
The drought was severe, but the farmers kept working.
The drought was severe, the farmers kept working.
The drought was severe farmers kept working.
questions.answer: The drought was severe, but the farmers kept working.

questions.text: Which is the most PRECISE and VIVID revision of: 'The dog ran across the field.'?
options: The animal moved fast.
The big dog ran far.
The shaggy border collie sprinted across the golden wheat field.
The dog ran quickly to the other side.
questions.answer: The shaggy border collie sprinted across the golden wheat field.

questions.text: In EXPOSITORY writing, a strong THESIS STATEMENT ___
options: tells an entertaining story
introduces the topic and states the main point of the essay
lists all the details the writer will use
thanks the reader for reading
questions.answer: introduces the topic and states the main point of the essay

questions.text: Which sentence uses CORRECT punctuation for a COMPLEX SENTENCE with a subordinate clause at the beginning?
options: When the rain finally came the farmers rejoiced.
When the rain finally came, the farmers rejoiced.
The farmers rejoiced, when the rain finally came.
When the rain finally came; the farmers rejoiced.
questions.answer: When the rain finally came, the farmers rejoiced.

questions.text: A NARRATIVE essay tells a story from the writer's own experience. A strong narrative includes ___
options: only facts and statistics
only dialogue between characters
specific details, sensory language, and a clear sequence of events
a persuasive argument and call to action
questions.answer: specific details, sensory language, and a clear sequence of events

questions.text: Identify the ERROR in this sentence: 'Each of the students have finished their test.'
options: 'Each' should be 'All'
'have' should be 'has' because 'Each' is singular
'their' should be 'its'
'finished' should be 'finishing'
questions.answer: 'have' should be 'has' because 'Each' is singular

questions.text: Which correctly uses an ADVERB to describe the verb?
options: The tired horse walked slow.
The tired horse walked slowly.
The tired horse walked more slower.
The tired horse walked most slowest.
questions.answer: The tired horse walked slowly.

questions.text: Which sentence uses a PREPOSITIONAL PHRASE to tell WHERE?
options: The rooster crowed loudly.
Before sunrise, she milked the cows.
The cattle grazed peacefully on the hillside.
She was very tired after working.
questions.answer: The cattle grazed peacefully on the hillside.

questions.text: When REVISING an essay for ORGANIZATION, a writer should check that ___
options: all words are spelled correctly
all sentences are the same length
ideas flow logically and transitions connect paragraphs
there are no commas used
questions.answer: ideas flow logically and transitions connect paragraphs

questions.text: Which word is NOT spelled correctly?
options: necessary
separate
begining
environment
questions.answer: begining

questions.text: Which sentence uses the CORRECT comparative form?
options: This summer was more hotter than last year.
This summer was more hot than last year.
This summer was hotter than last year.
This summer was most hotter than last year.
questions.answer: This summer was hotter than last year.

questions.text: Which transition phrase BEST introduces a CONCLUDING paragraph?
options: In addition
For example
First of all
In conclusion
questions.answer: In conclusion

questions.text: A COMPOUND SENTENCE contains ___
options: one independent clause and one dependent clause
two or more independent clauses joined by a conjunction
only one subject and one verb
a clause that cannot stand alone
questions.answer: two or more independent clauses joined by a conjunction

questions.text: Which sentence contains a DANGLING MODIFIER error?
options: Running through the field, the cows mooed at her.
Running through the field, she heard the cows mooing.
She heard the mooing cows as she ran through the field.
The cows mooed as she ran through the field.
questions.answer: Running through the field, the cows mooed at her.

questions.text: Which sentence BEST uses SENSORY DETAILS (details that appeal to the senses)?
options: It was hot outside.
The farm was nice.
The scorching sun baked the cracked earth as the scent of dry hay drifted through the still air.
The weather was bad that day.
questions.answer: The scorching sun baked the cracked earth as the scent of dry hay drifted through the still air.

questions.text: A colon (:) can be used to ___
options: join two unrelated sentences
introduce a list after a complete sentence
replace a period at the end of a sentence
show that a character is speaking
questions.answer: introduce a list after a complete sentence

questions.text: Which is the MOST EFFECTIVE introductory sentence for an essay about the importance of bees to Texas agriculture?
options: Bees are insects that live in hives.
This essay is about bees and Texas.
Without the tireless work of bees, billions of dollars in Texas crops would fail to grow — yet most Texans never give these tiny pollinators a second thought.
I am going to tell you about bees.
questions.answer: Without the tireless work of bees, billions of dollars in Texas crops would fail to grow — yet most Texans never give these tiny pollinators a second thought.
